title: Anthropic Sued By Sony, Warner For Allegedly Stealing Tens of Thousands of Songs, Torrenting Copyrighted Works
content:
Anthropic Sued By Sony, Warner For Allegedly Stealing Tens of Thousands of Songs, Torrenting Copyrighted Works (axios.com) 32
			
		 	
				 Axios reports:
Some of the world's largest music publishers filed a blockbuster lawsuit against Anthropic late Friday night, alleging "one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history." 
 
The suit is the opening salvo in what is now likely to be a yearslong fight over music, AI, and how intellectual property is protected in a new era of technology... The Sony/Warner lawsuit is notable because it's broad. It alleges Anthropic unlawfully trained its models off "tens of thousands" of music publishers' copyrighted compositions, whereas other lawsuits have focused on a narrower set of works. BMG's lawsuit against Anthropic, for example, claims infringement against 493 compositions.
 
What they're saying: "Defendants Anthropic and its founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann have conducted a brazen campaign of illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading copyrighted works on a massive scale in order to develop, operate, and reap enormous profits from Anthropic's 'Claude' series of artificial intelligence ('AI') models," the plaintiffs write in the 48-page complaint. They also claim that Anthropic pirated thousands of copyrighted musical works...
More details from The Verge: The companies are asking for up to $150,000 per work, plus up to $25,000 for each instance when identifiable copyright data was stripped. In total, the damages could amount to several billion dollars if a court finds in Sony and Warner's favor and awards the maximum amount...
 
The suit alleges that Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books, and that employees downloaded at least two million more from Pirate Library Mirror. It also claims that Anthropic scraped lyrics from sites like MusixMatch and LyricFind, which paid to license content from the labels.

report.summary: 索尼、华纳起诉Anthropic盗用数万首歌曲训练Claude，索赔或达数十亿美元。
report.background: 音乐出版商与AI公司的版权纠纷再度升级。Anthropic被指控使用BitTorrent下载超过五百万本盗版书籍，并抓取MusixMatch、LyricFind等已付费许可网站的歌词来训练其Claude模型。此前BMG已起诉Anthropic，但仅涉及493首作品；此次索尼、华纳联合诉讼覆盖“数万首”音乐作品，范围更广。原告要求每件作品最高15万美元赔偿，加上删除版权管理信息的罚款，总金额可能高达数十亿美元。这一案件被视为AI训练数据合规争议中的标志性事件，可能开启长达数年的法律拉锯战。
key_points: 诉讼指控Anthropic及其创始人通过非法torrent、抓取等方式大规模获取版权作品，涵盖数万首歌曲和数百万本盗版书籍。
相比BMG案仅涉及493首作品，索尼/华纳案覆盖“数万首”音乐作品，范围极广，可能成为AI版权诉讼的标杆。
原告要求每件作品最高15万美元赔偿，外加删除版权信息的罚款，索赔总额预计可达数十亿美元。
Anthropic被指从MusixMatch、LyricFind等已向唱片公司付费的网站抓取歌词，等于绕过授权直接使用内容。
案件可能迫使AI公司重新审视训练数据来源，推动行业建立更严格的版权合规与许可机制。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，此案将明确训练数据使用版权作品的边界，可能迫使AI公司支付版税或获得授权，显著增加训练成本。对开发者来说，开源模型和数据管道的版权审查将变得更重要，需要引入合规工具和法律评估。对普通用户，未来AI音乐生成、歌词问答等功能可能受限，或只能基于授权内容提供服务，相关产品价格也可能上升。总之，版权方与AI公司的博弈将深刻影响生成式AI的商业模式。
report.tools: 可关注Anthropic官方训练数据透明度报告、数据溯源审查工具（如Data Provenance Initiative）、版权追踪平台（如Copyright Clearance Center），以及AI训练数据审计框架（如WIMBD）来评估和降低版权风险。
